title: I built a free, open-source trading journal that auto-logs your trades using Voice AI. No more manual typing.
author: I1Youni
selftext:
Hey guys, I always hated journaling my trades because typing out the reasons, timeframe, and mistakes after closing a position felt like a chore. So I built TradeLog, an open-source voice-powered trading journal.

How it works:

Instead of typing, you just send a voice message to a Telegram bot (or use the web UI) while you are looking at the chart. You talk out loud about your setup, and the AI (Whisper + LLM) automatically extracts the data, fills the checklist, and saves it to the database.

Features:

Voice-to-JSON trade extraction (Supports Persian/Farsi out of the box, customizable for English).

Clean dashboard with PnL, Win Rate, and Balance.

Runs on GitHub Pages + Render + PostgreSQL (100% free hosting).

Fully open-source. 

You can host it yourself.

Check out the demo video and code here: https://github.com/I1Shady/Tradelog

I'd love to hear your feedback or if you want to contribute to the roadmap (like the upcoming Chart Image Analyzer).

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: voice right after the close is when the honest reasons come out, typed ones get cleaned up. what does it do when Whisper mishears a price, does it flag the number for you to confirm?

replies.author: I1Youni
replies.body: That's actually something I'm planning to handle in the Image Analyzer module, which I haven't implemented yet. The idea is to use the chart screenshot to help verify extracted trade data, especially important numbers like entry price, stop loss, and take profit. Thanks for bringing this up!

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: checking the extracted numbers against the screenshot makes sense for entry and stop. I'd still make it ask you whenever the two disagree, a wrong stop price sitting quietly in a journal is worse than a blank one.

replies.author: I1Youni
replies.body:
Yeah, that's a really good point! User confirmation should definitely be part of the process whenever there's a mismatch. I've added this to my list of things to work on in future updates.
My code is still in its early stages, and there are quite a few bugs to fix. But since this is my first project on GitHub, I decided to publish it and see what kind of feedback I get. I'll keep improving it step by step.
As the saying goes, every great piece of software was once a small program that simply worked. 😄
Thanks again for your suggestions! I really appreciate it. 🙏❤️

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: no rush on the bugs. a first project that already has a confirm step on its list is ahead of most journals I've tried.

replies.author: I1Youni
replies.body:
Thanks, man! I really appreciate the encouragement.  
I'm learning a lot through this project, and feedback like yours helps me see things I hadn't considered before. I'll keep improving it step by step! 🙏

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body: The confirmation step should probably be field-specific rather than asking users to approve the whole Voice-to-JSON record. Highlight low-confidence values from Whisper, especially entry, exit, size, and timeframe, then read those numbers back before saving to PostgreSQL. I’d also keep the original Telegram audio and extraction version beside every edit. That creates a useful error set for testing Persian/Farsi versus English and shows whether later LLM changes improve numeric accuracy instead of silently rewriting the journal.

replies.author: I1Youni
replies.body: That's a really great suggestion! I genuinely appreciate you taking the time to share your thoughts. I've saved your idea in my project ideas log so I can revisit it during development. Thanks a lot for helping me improve TradeLog. I really appreciate it!

comments.author: QATSAlgo
comments.body:
I’d treat voice/image extraction as proposed journal fields and reconcile price, size, fees and timestamps with execution records wherever possible. A screenshot can repeat the same mistaken number; an execution ID lets you trace corrections and partial fills. Keep the original note separate from the imported facts.



We’re QATS. If a prop-perpetuals import is useful for your roadmap, try our Trading API docs: [https://quantityproject.github.io/qats-trader-api/](https://quantityproject.github.io/qats-trader-api/) . There are orders, executions, positions and account/risk state for a dedicated adapter. History routes are capped, so don’t promise a gap-free full-history import. QATS evaluations and initial funded accounts are simulated; this is not an existing TradeLog integration.

comments.author: investigatormaker
comments.body:
For TradeLog, I'd add a confirmation step between voice extraction and saving: show the transcript beside the extracted entry, flag missing fields instead of guessing, and let traders correct it. For Persian/Farsi and English, test spoken numbers and long/short direction separately before extracted entries affect the PnL dashboard.
